children: new five-year business plan, due to be approved by its board on Monday, is expected to exceed $120 billion, more than 10% above the firm's current investment program, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Exploration and production (E&P) is expected to account for about 80% of planned investments, with increased funding for the Equatorial Margin, a frontier Petrobras sees as its most promising new oil province, according to the sources.
Petrobras declined to comment on the plan.
The current business plan earmarks about $2.5 billion for the Equatorial Margin, but the new program is expected to raise that amount after recent discoveries at the Morpho well.
"The business plan is very solid and very well structured and will come in between $120 billion and $125 billion," one source said on condition of anonymity.
A second source said discussions reflected Petrobras' project pipeline and existing commitments, pointing to investments "slightly above $120 billion."
The sources said this year's rise in oil prices, driven mainly by the Middle East conflict, was not a determining factor behind the larger spending plan.
The plan will target Brazilian diesel self-sufficiency by 2031 through refining investments, the sources said. The country currently produces about 70% of the diesel it consumes and imports the rest.
Higher global fuel prices this year increased pressure on the government, which resorted to tax breaks and subsidy measures to contain domestic costs.

Analysts at JPMorgan said investors broadly expected Petrobras' new business plan to feature higher spending than the current one, though market expectations were centered on roughly $115 billion to $120 billion in total investments.

JPMorgan said the key topic was whether additional capital would accelerate production growth and cash generation. "Higher capex is expected; the question is what shareholders get in return," the analysts said.
